Your edge isn't what your strategy makes. It's what's left after costs.

For an active F&O trader, the cost stack looks like this:
• Brokerage
• STT on options and futures
• Exchange transaction charges
• SEBI turnover fees
• GST on brokerage and charges
• Stamp duty
• Slippage, the cost that never appears on the contract note

For a strategy that trades many times a day, these can take a big share of gross profits. A strategy that looks great on paper can turn negative after costs.

What serious traders do:
→ Calculate net profit per trade, not gross
→ Run cost stress tests: what if costs rise by 20%?
→ Cut trade frequency if it isn't adding edge
→ Choose execution partners on total cost and fill quality, not only headline brokerage

Every rupee saved in costs goes straight to your bottom line, and that adds up over years.

Do you track your cost-to-profit ratio? What does it look like?
